title: Visual fallback lattice for staged rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Platform customers need a clearer, low-friction way to define and recover from staged rollout failures (canary + A/B). Existing canvases focus on traffic splits but do not make fallback paths and observable safety gates explicit in the same visual flow. This creates operational latency during incidents and leads to conservative rollouts that underutilize capacity.

Goal: Design a compact visual lattice that surfaces primary rollout paths, automatic fallback nodes, and escape hatches (immediate rollback, route to stable variant, divert to shadow) with clear affordances for thresholds, alerts, and required human approvals. The lattice should be compact enough for per-route dashboards yet expressive for multi-variant experiments.

This ticket covers: 1) low-fidelity and mid-fidelity lattice prototypes, 2) a clickable simulator for engineers to see simulated traffic and alarms, 3) a compact summary card for the per-route dashboard, and 4) review cycle with PM/Eng/Research for edge cases (cross-region failover, degradation vs correctness regressions).
acceptance_criteria:
- Prototype shows primary path + at least three fallback strategies with visual precedence (rollback, stable-variant, shadow).
- Designers have created a compact summary card (max 280px height) for the route dashboard that conveys current node, health, and next safe action.
- Simulator can play a 5-minute synthetic traffic trace and visualize thresholds crossing and automatic fallback.
- PM and Eng approved interaction model and escalation copy.
- Accessibility: color-blind safe palette and keyboard-only controls for activating fallback.
- Ready-to-handoff Figma file and a short design spec doc for eng implementation.
comments: 2026-02-27 Maya Chen: Uploaded initial low-fi lattice sketches and a short walkthrough video. Called out three fallback strategies and suggested default ordering: 1) divert to stable variant, 2) immediate rollback, 3) shadow/compare-only.

2026-03-02 Priya Singh: PM feedback - add a soft-alert state that requires review before auto-fallback for high-risk models (safety-sensitive routes). Also asked for copy suggestions for the human approval modal.

2026-03-04 Ethan Wright: Eng review - simulator approach looks feasible. Need explicit API contract for signals (latency, error-rate, accuracy delta). Called out dependency ENG-49823 for instrumentation.

2026-03-07 Zoe Park: Research - initial unmoderated test with 12 platform engineers. Key finding: users expect the lattice to show time-to-rollback and the most-likely contributor to failure. Added notes in research doc.
progress_updates: 2026-03-01 Low-fi pass complete; shared with PM/Eng for initial alignment.
2026-03-05 Mid-fi (componentized nodes) ready; implemented keyboard nav flows and color-blind palette variants.
2026-03-08 Clickable simulator built in Figma; includes a 5-minute synthetic trace and toggles for different alarm thresholds.
2026-03-10 Design review scheduled with Eng and PM; consolidated feedback captured and decisions recorded below.
decisions: Keep default fallback ordering as: divert-to-stable -> immediate-rollback -> shadow, because divert preserves user experience while rollback is irreversible.
Expose a per-route 'safety strictness' knob (low/medium/high) that maps to thresholds and whether human approval is required before fallback.
Make the summary card read-only by default with a prominent 'Open lattice' action to reduce accidental changes from the dashboard.
Use an icon + compact text lane to surface the reason for fallback (latency spike, error increase, quality regression).
next_steps: Iterate high-fidelity visuals and hand off components to frontend (link to component spec in Figma).
Work with Eng to define the signal contract for the runtime (ENG-49823 dependency).
Run a 1-hour moderated usability session with platform SREs to validate copy and emergency rollback affordances.
Prepare an implementation spike ticket for Dedicated capacity edge cases (ENG-52211).
